St. Isaac the Righteous

St. Isaac the Patriarch · St. Righteous Patriarch Isaac

Period
Biblical patriarchal period; no independently established absolute dates assigned here
Region
Canaan; Gerar; Beersheba
Titles / vocation
Righteous · Patriarch
Commemoration
Sunday of the Holy Forefathers (Sunday falling December 11–17 on the church calendar)

Introduction

St. Isaac, son of St. Abraham, belongs to the biblical covenant story and is commemorated among the righteous Patriarchs before Christ’s Nativity.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeathCommemoration and identityChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death at 180 in the biblical narrative; Genesis 35:28–29

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Isaac is the child promised to St. Abraham and his wife in old age. Genesis connects his birth with God’s covenant and later recounts the testing of Abraham, in which Isaac is bound for sacrifice but spared when God provides a ram.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 17:15–22; 21:1–5; 22:1–19

Life and notable events

Genesis describes his marriage, the birth of his two sons, and a period of famine. God renews the promise given to Abraham and commands Isaac to remain in the land. Disputes over wells and an agreement with a neighboring ruler form part of his life in Gerar and Beersheba. The account of the blessing of St. Jacob also records conflict and deception within the family.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 24:62–67; 25:19–28; 26:1–33; 27:1–40

Death

Genesis gives St. Isaac’s age at death as 180 and says that his sons bury him. The text presents a death in old age, not an execution or martyrdom. No modern absolute date is supplied by this profile.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Genesis 35:27–29

Commemoration and identity

The OCA names St. Isaac as a righteous Patriarch among Christ’s ancestors. His commemoration belongs to the movable Sundays before the Nativity, so the date displayed in a sample-year article should not be treated as fixed.

[3] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Named list of the holy Patriarchs

Hebrews recalls both the offering and Isaac’s blessing of the next generation. This Isaac is the Old Testament Patriarch, distinct from St. Isaac the Syrian and from the Abbot Isaac speaking in St. John Cassian’s Conferences.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Hebrews 11:17–20; Genesis 25:19–28
